summary: A Network Host Status report covering May 22 to June 2, 1972. No testing was done on Memorial Day or on May 31 and June 1, because of an attempt to install the new IMP system. Three new terminal IMPs were installed during the period. It was replaced by RFC 362.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 353 reports ARPANET host status from May 22 through June 2, 1972. It lists three Terminal IMP installations and explains why some days have no test results.

questions: which terminal imps does rfc 353 list
subtitle: A report of ARPANET host status from May 22 to June 2, 1972.

tldr.problem: ARPANET participants needed regular status information about hosts and network connections.
tldr.mechanism: The report provides host status and test tables for May 22 through June 2, noting testing gaps and three Terminal IMP installations.
tldr.outcome: RFC 353 updates RFC 344 and was later obsoleted by RFC 362.

today: RFC 353 updates RFC 344 and was later obsoleted by RFC 362.

sections.title: Reporting Period and Network Changes
sections.content:
The memo reports on most Network Hosts from May 22 to June 2. It records three Terminal IMP installations: number 155 at Fort Belvoir on June 1, number 154 at SAAC on June 3, and number 153 at NOAA on June 5.

No testing was done on May 29, which the memo identifies as Memorial Day in Massachusetts. Testing was also skipped on May 31 and June 1 during an attempt to install the new IMP system.
sections.plainLanguage: The report lists three Terminal IMP installations and several dates without testing. The missing tests were due to Memorial Day and an attempted IMP system installation.

sections.title: Host Tests and Status Codes
sections.content:
The tables give reported host roles and daily test results. The test codes include O for Open, D for Dead, H for Half Open, R for Refused, T for Timed out, and F for Full. Full means the host opened a connection but all Network ports were in use and it immediately closed the connection.

A timeout means a host did not complete the ICP and open a connection within 60 seconds. Marked entries indicate that a site had warned it might not be available at that time.
sections.plainLanguage: The test table records how each host responded. F means all Network ports were in use, while T means the host did not open within 60 seconds.

sections.title: User-Only Hosts and Status Reports
sections.content:
The memo identifies Terminal IMPs and the Network Control Center computer as excluded from daily testing because they were intended as users only or used to gather statistics. It also provides a separate table of host roles and predictions supplied by named contacts.

The report distinguishes those descriptions from the daily test results and marks some hosts as user-only, experimental servers, or expected to become servers later.
sections.plainLanguage: The report has one table of reported host roles and another of test results. User-only systems and the Network Control Center were excluded from daily tests.
